concreteFindings: Older matrix rows list 750 selected regional/reasoning IDs but omit inherited L1-L3 profiles, applications, sweetness distinctions, classification and legal recall. Those omitted IDs are separately enumerated by region/dimension below.
Existing dry/sweet Bordeaux, Alsace VT/SGN, Beaujolais early-release and Finger Lakes dry/sweet content was found; this addition uses those facts as prerequisites instead of reproducing them.
New York previously had no four-role regional case in its directly selected matrix cohort; the new Finger Lakes and Long Island cases supply separate white and red applications.

Olifants River was mapped geographically but the matched analytical inventory lacked its local growing-context principle. Two new site/water principles and a Chenin affordable-price scenario supply that specific context.

BC now has a site/cellar/quality/price/channel case beyond Ontario protection/drainage; Argentina adds distinct Salta, San Juan and Patagonia decisions beyond Mendoza; Portugal adds Tejo red, Setubal white/rose and Lisboa routes beyond the existing Tejo white and Setubal red cases.

externalPracticeRows.limitation: These are selected origin/classification and fictional channel applications, not a current-law audit for every regional group. Review primary rules, exact locators and commercial assumptions and map those dimensions region by region.
Inherited tasting principles and guided practice support observation and calibration. They do not establish accurate description of independently assessed real wines across the regional range.
Self-reviewed quality and ageing evidence supports practice, but no independent calibration result or assessed accuracy is supplied. More varied real wines and qualified feedback remain necessary.

The feature records three untimed actual-wine observations, comparison and self-review with physical acknowledgement. It does not provide an independently assessed blind tasting result or the full multi-flight assessment shape.

The default pack and two whole alternates provide nine original regional questions in app-specific 60-minute sessions. Broaden dimensional and regional variety, and obtain qualified calibration; self-review does not automatically grade prose or replicate an official examination.

An alternate timed whole pack now adds Burgundy lot evidence, Bordeaux harvest/blend/route and Loire–Rhone comparative reasoning. Further French styles, commercial contexts and qualified calibration remain; this is formative app practice.
